The held text of section 31, which makes the flag prescribed by EO 10798 the official flag until July 4, 1960 and makes the flag prescribed by Part I the official flag on that date. By its own terms the transition was complete on July 4, 1960, when the Part I flag became the official flag; the section says until July 4, 1960, so the exclusive reading is that the period of the earlier flag ended as that day began and the inclusive reading is that it ran through that day, and the order itself places the changeover on that date, which is recorded as the end. Clause exhausted by its own terms; the continuing predicate for the order comes from the other scopes.

The held text of section 33, which revokes Executive Order No. 10798 of January 3, 1959. It is a one-time revocation with no stated effective date other than the order itself, so it was performed on signing, 1959-08-21 (published 1959-08-25), and the clause is exhausted by performance on that date; the Code note records that EO 10798 was revoked by this section. The surviving consequence, that EO 10798 stays revoked, is not a continuing command of this order.

research_rationale:
EO 10834 (Eisenhower, signed 1959-08-21, 24 FR 6865, published 1959-08-25) was issued on the admission of Hawaii and prescribes the design of the flag with fifty stars (Part I: sections 1 to 3, with the position of stars and the proportions set out in an attachment made part of the order), the sizes of flags authorized for executive agencies and rules for their procurement (Part II: sections 21 to 25) and general provisions (Part III: section 31 making the flag of EO 10798 official until July 4, 1960 and the Part I flag official on that date, section 32 defining executive agencies, and section 33 revoking EO 10798). The dossier inventory omitted section 1, ran section 3 across about 7,900 characters of Federal Register front matter, split the section 21 size table into row fragments and omitted sections 22 to 24 and 31 to 32 as separate scopes, so the inventory is corrected with overrides to eleven scopes covering every section of the held text. Sections 31 and 33 are spent by their own terms: section 33 revoked EO 10798 on signing, and section 31 provided for the changeover on July 4, 1960 (the order states no other effective date, and 4 U.S.C. 2, recited in the order, fixes July 4 as the effective date of an added star). The remaining sections have no term or condition. The held Code prints the whole order as a current note, with no amendment, under 4 U.S.C. 1, and 4 U.S.C. 5 still defines the flag by reference to it. The Federal Register disposition note lists no amendment or revocation of EO 10834 itself. The order rests on the President's authority as President and Commander in Chief and on the Federal Property and Administrative Services Act of 1949, which the Code bracket shows is now codified in chapters 1 to 11 of title 40 and division C of subtitle I of title 41; the text of those provisions is not held, so the claim relies on the Code's continued printing of the order and on 4 U.S.C. 5.

savings.reason: The design and procurement rules continue; the two spent clauses (the changeover on July 4, 1960 and the revocation of EO 10798) leave no residual command. Flags procured under earlier contracts are covered by section 25, which stays operative.
